att_op_current_state.user_query: How does this work today, without the workbench?
att_op_current_state.ai_message: Today the cycle opens with 207 anomalies and no grouping. You pull the billing, rate-card, tax and account reports, and they do not reconcile with each other, so every anomaly becomes a small investigation: is this a real error or a legitimate change the customer made? Real ones get corrected one account at a time; unclear ones get escalated and lose a day. Then the 36-hour window closes and whatever did not fit becomes next cycle's credits, calls and disputes. The friction is not detection — it is that trusting a fix costs more time than making it.

att_op_future_state.user_query: Where does the workbench change the picture?
att_op_future_state.ai_message: Five interventions. Reconciling disagreeing reports becomes one fused cycle view you can ask questions of. Investigating each anomaly by hand becomes six pattern decisions with a named root cause. Deciding whether a correction is safe becomes per-account confidence plus current-versus-corrected reconciliation. Correcting one account at a time becomes Apply Fix to All with rebill IDs written as you act. And finding out downstream that you were late becomes a projection of calls prevented against the SLA clock. The investigation moves to the system; the decision stays with you.

att_op_journey.ai_message: Four phases. The cycle opens and you need scope and a clock — 207 anomalies, $4,850 at risk, 91.6% confidence, 11.7 hours left. Then you need the anomalies to stop feeling random: six patterns, each with a cause you can act on. Then the hard part, trusting the fix: named root cause, 94% confidence, and a per-account preview of current versus corrected. Then you act and prove it: Apply Fix to All for 87 accounts and $850.14, with rebill IDs and a governance log written as you go. The moments that matter are 207 becoming 6, the root cause making a bulk fix feel safe, and one click landing in an audit trail.
